newsitem.title: CANADA: Expeditors says seeking organic growth.
newsitem.headline: Expeditors says seeking organic growth.

text.p: Expeditors International, the Seattle-based global freight forwarder, will continue to favour organic growth rather than be tempted into major acquisitions to sustain its impressive earnings growth, chairman Peter Rose told Reuters.
Earlier this week, Expeditors' announced second quarter after-tax earnings rose 52 percent to a record $8.17 million. Net revenues rose 45 percent.

Americans love to cheer on the underdog and cheer when the mighty stumble, said Rose in a telephone interview, so it will not be easy for Expeditors to retain the favour of stock markets, possibly even customers.
Recently, one customer suggested to Rose a very profitable forwarder like Expeditors could afford to absorb carrier rate increases instead of passing them on to customers.
"That's a ticket to bankruptcy," said the Canadian-born Rose, adding he does not expect most customers will have any problem accepting Expeditors' success.
Expeditors' earnings have exceeded the forecasts of financial analysts on so many occasions it may be harder to keep expectations in line, said Rose.
Analysts now listen to the company's near-term projections and little else. What Rose would like them to hear is the company will stick with its patient growth strategy.

Rose said the company's solid second quarter gains were due to the strong performance of its mature operations, a strong economy, stringent cost control and talented people. Buying market share did not figure into the equation.

"We didn't go out on this acquisitions thing a few years ago," says Rose, a reference to competitors like San Francisco-based forwarder Fritz Cos, which grew rapidly through acquisitions in mid-decade and then suffered a sharp earnings decline last year.
Even internally, said Rose, there used to be questions raised about why Expeditors did not imitate Fritz.

"In hindsight, we were doing exactly the right thing," he said. "Everything we've done has always been more calculated. We've always been willing to take a step backwards in order to take two forward."
Expeditors is eyeing further growth in Latin America, where its only offices are in Brazil and Chile. Brazil has yet to turn a profit. "They are close," but not there yet, said Rose.
Near-term expansion targets include Argentina, Venezuela, Costa Rica and possibly Peru.

In mature markets like the UK, the company has done well with new satellite offices opened in markets near London like Bedford and Swindon. It is implanting the satellite concept in France and plans satellites in Germany and Italy.
Its one recent acquisition was Irish forwarder SeaSky, which gave it profitable operations in Dublin, Cork and Shannon.
